# Code Documentation in C#

Welcome! I'd be happy to help you learn about code documentation in C#. Coming from Dart, you'll find C# documentation quite powerful and well-integrated with tooling.

## XML Documentation Comments in C#


In C#, we use **XML Documentation Comments** (also called XML doc comments) that start with `///` (triple forward slash). These are similar to Dart's `///` doc comments, but C# uses XML tags for structure.


## Basic Syntax


Here's the fundamental structure:

```csharp
/// <summary>
/// Brief description of what this does
/// </summary>
public class MyClass { }
```


## Common XML Tags


Here are the most frequently used documentation tags:

```csharp
/// <summary>
/// Main description of the member
/// </summary>
/// <param name="parameterName">Description of parameter</param>
/// <returns>Description of return value</returns>
/// <exception cref="ExceptionType">When this exception is thrown</exception>
/// <remarks>Additional information or notes</remarks>
/// <example>
/// Usage example with code
/// <code>
/// var instance = new MyClass();
/// instance.DoSomething();
/// </code>
/// </example>
```


## Complete Class Documentation Example


```csharp
namespace MedicalImaging
{
    /// <summary>
    /// Represents a DICOM image with metadata and pixel data
    /// </summary>
    /// <remarks>
    /// This class provides functionality to load, process, and analyze
    /// medical images in DICOM format commonly used in radiology
    /// </remarks>
    public class DicomImage
    {
        /// <summary>
        /// Gets or sets the patient identifier
        /// </summary>
        /// <value>The unique patient ID from the DICOM header</value>
        public string PatientId { get; set; }

        /// <summary>
        /// Gets the image width in pixels
        /// </summary>
        public int Width { get; private set; }

        /// <summary>
        /// Loads a DICOM image from the specified file path
        /// </summary>
        /// <param name="filePath">The full path to the DICOM file</param>
        /// <returns>A new instance of DicomImage containing the loaded data</returns>
        /// <exception cref="ArgumentNullException">Thrown when filePath is null</exception>
        /// <exception cref="FileNotFoundException">Thrown when the file doesn't exist</exception>
        /// <example>
        /// <code>
        /// var image = DicomImage.LoadFromFile("/path/to/image.dcm");
        /// Console.WriteLine($"Patient: {image.PatientId}");
        /// </code>
        /// </example>
        public static DicomImage LoadFromFile(string filePath)
        {
            if (filePath == null)
                throw new ArgumentNullException(nameof(filePath));
            
            // Implementation here
            return new DicomImage();
        }

        /// <summary>
        /// Applies a Gaussian filter to smooth the image
        /// </summary>
        /// <param name="sigma">The standard deviation of the Gaussian kernel</param>
        /// <param name="kernelSize">The size of the convolution kernel (must be odd)</param>
        /// <returns>A new DicomImage with the filter applied</returns>
        /// <remarks>
        /// This method is useful for noise reduction before edge detection
        /// or other image processing operations
        /// </remarks>
        public DicomImage ApplyGaussianFilter(double sigma = 1.0, int kernelSize = 3)
        {
            // Implementation
            return new DicomImage();
        }
    }
}
```


## Documentation for Different Members


### Constructors


```csharp
/// <summary>
/// Initializes a new instance of the <see cref="DicomImage"/> class
/// </summary>
/// <param name="width">Image width in pixels</param>
/// <param name="height">Image height in pixels</param>
public DicomImage(int width, int height)
{
    Width = width;
    Height = height;
}
```

### Interfaces


```csharp
/// <summary>
/// Defines operations for medical image processing algorithms
/// </summary>
public interface IImageProcessor
{
    /// <summary>
    /// Processes the input image and returns the result
    /// </summary>
    /// <param name="input">The source image to process</param>
    /// <returns>The processed image</returns>
    DicomImage Process(DicomImage input);
}
```

### Enums


```csharp
/// <summary>
/// Specifies the imaging modality type
/// </summary>
public enum ImagingModality
{
    /// <summary>
    /// Computed Tomography
    /// </summary>
    CT,
    
    /// <summary>
    /// Magnetic Resonance Imaging
    /// </summary>
    MRI,
    
    /// <summary>
    /// Digital Radiography (X-Ray)
    /// </summary>
    DX
}
```


## Advanced Documentation Features


### Cross-References with `<see>` and `<seealso>`


```csharp
/// <summary>
/// Analyzes the image using AI models
/// </summary>
/// <param name="image">The image to analyze</param>
/// <returns>Analysis results</returns>
/// <seealso cref="DicomImage"/>
/// <seealso href="https://www.dicomstandard.org/">DICOM Standard</seealso>
/// <remarks>
/// This method uses the <see cref="IImageProcessor"/> interface
/// to apply various processing steps before analysis
/// </remarks>
public AnalysisResult Analyze(DicomImage image) { }
```

### Generic Types Documentation


```csharp
/// <summary>
/// Represents a collection of medical images
/// </summary>
/// <typeparam name="T">The type of image, must inherit from DicomImage</typeparam>
public class ImageCollection<T> where T : DicomImage
{
    /// <summary>
    /// Adds an image to the collection
    /// </summary>
    /// <param name="image">The image to add</param>
    public void Add(T image) { }
}
```


## Generating Documentation


To generate documentation from your XML comments:

1. **Enable XML documentation file** in your `.csproj`:

```xml
<PropertyGroup>
    <GenerateDocumentationFile>true</GenerateDocumentationFile>
    <DocumentationFile>bin\$(Configuration)\$(TargetFramework)\$(AssemblyName).xml</DocumentationFile>
</PropertyGroup>
```

2. **Use tools** to generate HTML documentation:
   - **DocFX**: Microsoft's documentation generator
   - **Sandcastle**: Another popular option
   - **Swagger/OpenAPI**: For Web APIs

Example with DocFX:
```bash
# Install DocFX
dotnet tool install -g docfx

# Initialize documentation project
docfx init -q

# Build documentation
docfx build
```

## Best Practices


1. **Always document public APIs** - All public classes, methods, properties
2. **Be concise in `<summary>`** - Keep it to one or two sentences
3. **Use `<remarks>` for details** - Extended explanations go here
4. **Document exceptions** - Especially important for library code
5. **Include examples** - Help users understand usage quickly
6. **Use proper cref attributes** - For type-safe references


## Quick Tips for VS Code


Since you use VS Code, you can:

- Type `///` above any member to auto-generate the documentation template
- Install the "C# XML Documentation Comments" extension for better support
- Use snippets like `summary` after typing `///`

This documentation becomes especially valuable when:

- Your code is consumed as a NuGet package
- Working in teams
- Using tools that generate API documentation
- Getting IntelliSense help while coding
